correctness.rationale: For any three support normals separated by 120 degrees, summing the three line equations cancels the incenter term and makes the equilateral-triangle inradius the arithmetic mean of the support values. The regular-polygon support function is the circumradius times the cosine of angular distance to the vertex-direction lattice. If three divides the side count, the three phases coincide modulo that lattice. Otherwise the phases are exactly zero and plus/minus one third of a vertex spacing after reduction, so their sum is one cosine times a constant. This proves the full intervals, equality orientations, and the two asymptotic constants. The bundled checker reconstructs the triangles from vertex maxima and line intersections.
risks: The finite checker is diagnostic only; the universal statement rests on the exact support-phase proof.

value.rationale: The direct literature treats the inradius function of all circumscribed equilateral triangles as a circle-rigidity diagnostic. Regular polygons are the canonical discrete approximants to a circle, so their exact orientation dependence is a natural benchmark. The result gives the complete one-parameter range for every side count, extends beyond the prior-covered n=3k minimum endpoint, and reveals a sharp modulo-three arithmetic transition whose leading orientation oscillations differ by a factor of nine.
risks: The result is restricted to equilateral support triangles and does not solve the unrestricted minimum-enclosing-triangle problem for n not divisible by three.
